clue.text: State of electric current after link severed

indicators.note: the current symbol follows the word for link

parts.note: to link two things is to connect them
I is the physics symbol for electric current
something severed has been cut

explanation.surface: A cut cable leaves someone puzzled about the state of the electric supply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State' looks like a verb or a condition, but it is the definition: a US state.
explanation.definitionFit: Connecticut is one of the New England states of the USA.

clue.text: Rival bid in which location of tender appears illegal?

definitions.text: Rival bid in which location of tender appears illegal?

parts.words: Rival bid in which location of tender appears illegal?
parts.note: a rival bid is a counter-bid; money is tendered at a shop counter, and illegal dealings are done under the counter

explanation.surface: A competing offer in a contract tender looks dodgy.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as a whole: an offer made at the counter (where cash is tendered), and 'illegal' hints at under-the-counter dealing.
explanation.definitionFit: A rival offer made in reply to an earlier one is exactly what a counter-offer is.

clue.text: Sailor, Russian, raised by reptile

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means the word is written bottom to top

parts.note: Ivan is a stock Russian man's name
gator is short for alligator

explanation.surface: A Russian seaman brought up by an alligator.
explanation.definitionFit: A navigator steers a ship, so is a kind of seafarer.

clue.text: Turkey cut up to go round further

indicators.note: the reversed word surrounds the abbreviation for the country
in a down clue, up means the word is written bottom to top

parts.note: to axe something is to cut it
TR is the international vehicle code for Turkey

explanation.surface: Instructions for carving the turkey so the meat stretches further.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turkey' looks like the bird being carved; it is the country, by its vehicle code. 'up' turns the cut word to EXA, and 'to go round' wraps it about the code.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean additional, more than the usual amount.

clue.text: Bird changes colouring

parts.note: something that changes turns, as milk turns
a tone is a shade or tint of colour

explanation.surface: A bird that changes its plumage colour with the season.
explanation.definitionFit: The turnstone is a small wading shore bird that flips stones to find food.

clue.text: E.g. Hamlet makes one sad, timelessly uplifting

indicators.note: in a down clue, uplifting means the word is written bottom to top
T stands for time, so time is removed from the word

parts.note: something tragic makes one sad

explanation.surface: Shakespeare's Hamlet is a sad play, yet strangely uplifting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'timelessly' takes T out of TRAGIC to leave RAGIC; 'uplifting' turns that round. Hamlet is a well-known British cigar brand.
explanation.definitionFit: Hamlet is a brand of small cigars, so it is an example of one.

clue.text: Cream? You may find some here!

definitions.text: Cream? You may find some here!

parts.words: Cream? You may find some here!
parts.note: the cream of anything is the very best, and a cat that has had the cream may have some left on its whiskers

explanation.surface: A puzzle about where to find cream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cream' means the best, an idiom with the same sense as the answer, while a cat licking up cream often leaves some on its face.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means the very best, just as the cream is the finest part.

clue.text: Judge point of view to upset

parts.note: an angle is a perspective or viewpoint

explanation.surface: A judge's point of view seems designed to upset people.
explanation.definitionFit: To jangle someone's nerves is to unsettle or irritate them.

clue.text: Checked raising of French marine force

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising means the word is written bottom to top

parts.note: de is the French word for of
a tide is a force of the sea

explanation.surface: Someone checked on the raising of a French naval force.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raising' turns DETIDE upside down in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: Text that has been edited has been gone over and corrected.

clue.text: A tremble, giving away hesitation — what you're looking for is spirit

indicators.note: the word for tremble gives up the hesitation sound, which leaves it

parts.note: a quaver is a trembling in the voice
er is the sound of hesitation
in hide-and-seek terms, the one you are seeking is 'it'

explanation.surface: A shaky searcher drops the hesitation and finds the spirit they seek.
explanation.walkthrough: 'giving away' drops ER from QUAVER, leaving QUAV.
explanation.definitionFit: Aquavit is a Scandinavian caraway-flavoured spirit.

clue.text: First person in collective was angry about threat to crops?

indicators.note: the word for was angry goes around the pronoun

parts.note: to have raged is to have been angry
we is the first person plural pronoun

explanation.surface: The leader of a farm collective was furious about some danger to crops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First person in collective' looks like the group's leader, but it means the first-person plural pronoun; 'about' puts the word for was angry around it.
explanation.definitionFit: Ragwort-type weeds invade fields and spoil harvests, so they menace crops.

clue.text: Approach singer to retire

parts.note: to go to someone is to approach them
a grass is an informer, one who sings to the police

explanation.surface: Someone approaches a singer about bowing out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'singer' is slang for an informer, as is grass.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom, from horses put out to pasture, meaning to withdraw from active work.

clue.text: Dish of a sort, cooked

indicators.note: cooked here means the letters are cooked up into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A dish of some kind, prepared and served.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' signals reshuffling the letters of A SORT.
explanation.definitionFit: A joint of meat cooked in the oven is a classic dish.

clue.text: Leggy bird to welcome centre forward

indicators.note: the middle letter of the word is brought to the front

parts.note: to greet is to welcome

explanation.surface: A football club welcomes a lanky new centre forward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'centre forward' looks like a football position; it moves the middle E of GREET to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Egrets are long-legged wading herons.

clue.text: It's natural to get out of work if not challenged

indicators.note: the word for natural gets outside the word for work, enclosing it

parts.note: a natural photo or pose is unposed
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Skipping work comes naturally if nobody objects.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to get out of' looks like dodging work, but it puts UNPOSED outside OP.
explanation.definitionFit: A candidate standing without rivals faces no opposition.

clue.text: Don't bake enough, coming in for criticism

definitions.meaning: to fire pottery too little in the kiln
being attacked or censured, as by enemy guns

explanation.surface: A baker's undercooked loaves draw complaints.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as one word it means firing too little; as two it means facing attack.

clue.text: Pub bloomer picked up — they can be observed

parts.note: PH stands for public house on maps

indicators.note: in a down clue, picked up means the word is lifted to read bottom to top

parts.note: an anemone is a flower, something that blooms

explanation.surface: A pub gaffe is noticed by onlookers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' suggests a blunder, but here it is a flower; 'picked up' looks like a sound clue but turns ANEMONE into ENOMENA.
explanation.definitionFit: Phenomena are observable facts or events.

clue.text: React badly about dodgy grid that's filled with ink

indicators.note: the first rearrangement goes around the second
badly signals the word react is put together badly, rearranged
dodgy signals the word grid is unsound and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone reacts badly to a faulty crossword grid covered in ink.
explanation.walkthrough: Two separate anagrams: 'badly' gives CARTE and 'dodgy' gives RIDG, and 'about' sets the first around the second, so the grid of the surface is only fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A printer cartridge is a replaceable container of ink.

clue.text: Out of sorts, express sadness about university offer?

indicators.note: the word for weeping goes around the grades

parts.note: to cry is to express sadness
a conditional university offer in the UK asks for A-level grades such as ABB

explanation.surface: A grumpy applicant weeps over a university offer.
explanation.walkthrough: UK universities offer places on condition of A-level grades, written as letters like ABB.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone crabby is irritable and grumpy.

clue.text: That group's back to front way of thinking

indicators.note: the last letter is taken from the back and put at the front

parts.note: those refers to that group of things

explanation.surface: That group has a backward way of thinking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back to front' looks like reversal, but only the final E of THOSE moves to the start.
explanation.definitionFit: An ethos is a characteristic outlook or set of values.

clue.text: Remix it as New York State of Mind

indicators.note: a remix rearranges a song, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An instruction to remix the song Empire State of Mind, nodding to New York.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface echoes the songs 'New York State of Mind' and 'Empire State of Mind'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sanity is a sound mental condition.

clue.text: Like photo showing gel

parts.note: as can mean like, in the same way
pic is short for picture or photo

explanation.surface: A photo showing hair gel, or gel shown as in a picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Aspic is a savoury jelly made from meat stock.

clue.text: Sound found in Arabic language

indicators.note: the answer is found within the run of letters in these words

explanation.surface: A sound found in the Arabic language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found in' marks the letters spanning the two words.
explanation.definitionFit: A clang is a loud ringing metallic noise.

clue.text: A portion's unhealthy!

indicators.note: unhealthy signals the letters are in poor shape and rearranged

explanation.surface: An exclamation that a serving is bad for you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unhealthy' rearranges A PORTIONS; the whole clue also describes the answer, since any helping of it is harmful.
explanation.definitionFit: Rodent bait is poison, so any portion of it is bad for you.

clue.text: Burning up, holding roman candle

indicators.note: the reversed word holds the abbreviation inside it
in a down clue, up means the word is written bottom to top

parts.note: something burning is hot
RC is the abbreviation for Roman Catholic

explanation.surface: A Roman candle firework burning upwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roman candle' reads as one firework, but 'roman' gives RC and 'candle' is the definition; 'up' turns HOT into TOH, which holds RC.
explanation.definitionFit: A torch or candle is a source of light that burns.

clue.text: Useless batsman — tail-ender out for one in Indian side?

indicators.note: useless signals the batsman's letters are in a mess and rearranged
the last letter of the word is dismissed and replaced

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A cricket report: a useless tail-ender is out for one run, playing for an Indian team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tail-ender out for one' swaps the final N of BATSMAN for I; 'Useless' rearranges the result. In cricket, a tail-ender is a weak batsman who goes in last.
explanation.definitionFit: Basmati rice is served as a side dish with Indian food.

clue.text: Put up again after changing sides halfway, and get in again

indicators.note: the right sign in the middle of the word changes to left, R becoming L

parts.note: to re-erect something is to put it up again

explanation.surface: Someone is put up again as candidate after switching parties midway, and wins again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put up again' looks like the definition but gives RE-ERECT; R (right) halfway along becomes L (left).
explanation.definitionFit: To be voted back into office is to be returned by the voters once more.

clue.text: One making recording tails rival, at which they dispute?

parts.note: a logger records data
in a coin toss, heads is the alternative to tails

explanation.surface: A recorder trails a competitor in an argument.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition completes the idiom: people in dispute are said to be at loggerheads.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase 'at loggerheads' means in strong disagreement.
